In 2012, a team of Australian and French oceanographers aboard the research vessel Southern Surveyor set a course into the Coral Sea, northwest of New Caledonia. Their target: an island the size of Manhattan that had appeared on nautical charts since the 1870s. It had been faithfully reproduced in the Times Atlas of the World, included by the National Geographic Society in reference publications, and — until the morning of departure — listed on Google Maps with its own label and approximate coordinates.
When the vessel arrived, the ship's echo sounder showed 1,400 metres of open ocean. There was no island. There had never been an island. The most probable explanation: a 19th-century whaling ship had encountered a large raft of floating pumice or sea foam, logged it as a land sighting, and entered the coordinates into the official record. Subsequent chart-makers had copied from earlier charts without verification, and the error had compounded itself across 140 years and dozens of authoritative publications.
After the findings were published, Google quietly deleted the entry. The island had been present on official maps for longer than most living nations have existed.
What is the general term for mountains, islands, and rivers that appear in historical maps and atlases but have no physical existence? And what was the specific name of this non-existent Coral Sea island?
Phantom island, ghost island , sandy island all are correct
